objects.definition: typedef unsigned char sixel_index_t;
objects.description: Unsigned 8-bit index type used for palette indices or similar. Only the alias is defined here.

objects.definition: typedef int SIXELSTATUS;
objects.description: Integer status/result code type used by the API. Constants like SIXEL_OK, SIXEL_FALSE, and specific error-category flags are defined as macros in this header.

objects.definition: typedef void *(* sixel_malloc_t)(size_t);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom malloc-like allocator taking a size and returning a void*.

objects.definition: typedef void *(* sixel_calloc_t)(size_t, size_t);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom calloc-like allocator taking a count and element size and returning a void*.

objects.definition: typedef void *(* sixel_realloc_t)(void *, size_t);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom realloc-like allocator taking an existing pointer and a new size.

objects.definition: typedef void (* sixel_free_t)(void *);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom free-like deallocator taking a pointer to free.

objects.definition: struct sixel_allocator;
objects.description: Opaque allocator object that wraps user-provided allocation routines and reference counting. The struct is incomplete here; it is managed via API functions.

objects.definition: typedef int (* sixel_write_function)(char *data, int size, void *priv);
objects.description: Callback type for writing encoded SIXEL byte chunks. Returns int status; data/size specify the buffer; priv is user data.

objects.definition: struct sixel_output;
objects.description: Opaque output context for controlling SIXEL emission (7/8-bit, GRI arg limit, penetrator, DCS envelope, palette type, encode policy).

objects.definition: struct sixel_dither;
objects.description: Opaque dither/quantization context managing palette generation, diffusion, pixelformat, transparency, and related parameters.

objects.definition: typedef void * (* sixel_allocator_function)(size_t size);
objects.description: Allocator function pointer used by deprecated sixel_decode; single-argument malloc-like signature.

objects.definition: struct sixel_frame;
objects.description: Opaque image frame container holding pixels, palette, dimensions, pixelformat, transparency, timing and loop information; supports resize/clip/strip alpha.
Callback type invoked by sixel_helper_load_image_file to supply loaded image data into a sixel_frame along with user context.

objects.definition: struct sixel_encoder;
objects.description: Opaque easy-encoder object managing options, cancel flag, and encoding operations from files or raw bytes to SIXEL, writing via an internal output sink.

objects.definition: struct sixel_decoder;
objects.description: Opaque easy-decoder object managing options and performing decoding from stdin or files to frames/pixels via its API.

functions.name: sixel_allocator_new
functions.signature: SIXELSTATUS sixel_allocator_new(sixel_allocator_t **ppallocator, sixel_malloc_t fn_malloc, sixel_calloc_t fn_calloc, sixel_realloc_t fn_realloc, sixel_free_t fn_free);
functions.description: Creates a sixel_allocator_t object with optional custom allocation functions (malloc, calloc, realloc, free). Use this when you need to plug in custom memory management; pass NULLs for functions you don’t override (library will use defaults).
requirements: ppallocator must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the created allocator object.
fn_malloc/fn_calloc/fn_realloc/fn_free are function pointers compatible with the typedefs; they may be NULL to use defaults.
On success returns SIXEL_OK; on failure returns an error status; caller must check return value.
The created allocator must later be released via sixel_allocator_unref when no longer needed.

functions.name: sixel_allocator_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of an allocator object. Thread-unsafe; serialize externally if needed.
requirements: allocator must be a valid, previously created allocator object.
Caller must ensure thread-safety (function is thread-unsafe).
Each call to sixel_allocator_ref should be balanced with a matching sixel_allocator_unref.

functions.name: sixel_allocator_unref
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of an allocator object and destroys it when the count reaches zero. Thread-unsafe.
requirements: allocator must be a valid allocator pointer obtained from sixel_allocator_new.
Caller must ensure thread-safety (function is thread-unsafe).
After the final unref, the allocator pointer becomes invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: sixel_allocator_malloc
functions.description: Allocates n bytes using the allocator’s malloc implementation.
requirements: allocator must be a valid allocator (may be NULL only if documented by implementation; header suggests passing a valid object).
n is the number of bytes to allocate; large values may fail (library defines SIXEL_ALLOCATE_BYTES_MAX as an upper limit constant).
Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must check the result.

functions.name: sixel_allocator_calloc
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized memory for an array using the allocator’s calloc implementation.
requirements: allocator must be a valid allocator object.
nelm and elsize specify the number of elements and element size; their product must not overflow size_t.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check the result.

functions.name: sixel_allocator_realloc
functions.description: Reallocates the buffer p to size n using the allocator’s realloc implementation.
requirements: allocator must be a valid allocator object.
p may be NULL to behave like malloc; otherwise must be a pointer previously allocated by the same allocator.
n is the new size; may be zero to free memory depending on implementation.
Returns NULL on failure; on failure the original block remains valid and unchanged.

functions.name: sixel_allocator_free
functions.description: Frees a buffer allocated by the allocator’s allocation functions.
requirements: allocator must be a valid allocator object.
p must be a pointer previously returned by this allocator’s allocation functions or NULL.
After freeing, p must not be used.

functions.name: sixel_output_new
functions.signature: SIXELSTATUS sixel_output_new(sixel_output_t **output, sixel_write_function fn_write, void *priv, sixel_allocator_t *allocator);
functions.description: Creates a new output context that emits SIXEL data via the provided write callback. Use to control encoding output destination and options.
requirements: output must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the created output object.
fn_write must be a valid callback of type int(char *data, int size, void *priv) that returns an int status; it will be called with data chunks to write.
priv is user data passed to fn_write; can be NULL.
allocator may be NULL to use the default allocator or a valid allocator object.
Returns SIXEL_OK on success; caller must check return value and later destroy/unref the object.

functions.name: sixel_output_create
functions.description: Deprecated constructor for an output context using default allocation. Prefer sixel_output_new. It sets up a write callback and private data.
requirements: fn_write must be a valid write callback; see sixel_write_function.
priv is user data for the callback and may be NULL.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check the result.
Destroy/unref the returned object when done.

functions.name: sixel_output_destroy
functions.description: Destroys an output context object immediately. Prefer using unref if reference counting is used.
requirements: output must be a valid output context pointer created by sixel_output_new/create.
After destruction, the pointer must not be used.
Do not call if other references exist (use unref semantics appropriately).

functions.name: sixel_output_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of an output context. Thread-unsafe.
requirements: output must be a valid output context.
Function is thread-unsafe; callers must serialize access.
Balance each ref with an unref.

functions.name: sixel_output_unref
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of an output context, destroying it when the count reaches zero. Thread-unsafe.
requirements: output must be a valid output context.
Function is thread-unsafe; callers must serialize access.
After the final unref, the object is destroyed and must not be used.

functions.name: sixel_output_get_8bit_availability
functions.description: Returns whether the output is configured to use 8-bit C1 control characters (1) or 7-bit mode (0).
requirements: output must be a valid output context object.
Return value is an int flag: 0 means do not use 8-bit characters; 1 means use 8-bit characters.

functions.name: sixel_output_set_8bit_availability
functions.description: Configures whether to use 8-bit C1 control characters in the output stream.
requirements: output must be a valid output context.
availability must be 0 (do not use 8-bit characters) or 1 (use 8-bit characters).

functions.name: sixel_output_set_gri_arg_limit
functions.description: Sets whether to limit DECGRI('!') arguments to 255, for compatibility with some terminals.
requirements: output must be a valid output context.
value must be 0 (do not limit) or 1 (limit to 255).

functions.name: sixel_output_set_penetrate_multiplexer
functions.description: Enables or disables GNU Screen penetration using DCS pass-through sequences.
requirements: output must be a valid output context.
penetrate must be 0 (penetrate GNU Screen) or 1 (do not penetrate GNU Screen).

functions.name: sixel_output_set_skip_dcs_envelope
functions.description: Controls whether to skip emitting the DCS envelope around SIXEL data.
requirements: output must be a valid output context.
skip must be 0 (output DCS envelope) or 1 (do not output DCS envelope).

functions.name: sixel_output_set_palette_type
functions.description: Sets the palette color space used for output (RGB or HLS).
requirements: output must be a valid output context.
palettetype must be one of the PALETTETYPE_* constants (e.g., SIXEL_PALETTETYPE_RGB or SIXEL_PALETTETYPE_HLS).

functions.name: sixel_output_set_encode_policy
functions.description: Sets the encoding policy for SIXEL output (e.g., auto, fast, or size).
requirements: output must be a valid output context.
encode_policy must be one of SIXEL_ENCODEPOLICY_* constants.

functions.name: sixel_dither_new
functions.description: Creates a dither context used for color quantization and diffusion during encoding.
requirements: ppdither must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the dither object.
ncolors is the required number of colors; must be within library limits (SIXEL_PALETTE_MIN..SIXEL_PALETTE_MAX).
allocator may be NULL to use the default allocator or a valid allocator object.
Returns SIXEL_OK on success; caller must check the result and later destroy/unref the object.

functions.name: sixel_dither_create
functions.description: Deprecated constructor for a dither context with the given number of colors. Prefer sixel_dither_new.
requirements: ncolors is the desired palette size; must be within supported range.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check and later destroy/unref the object.

functions.name: sixel_dither_get
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a built-in dither configuration by ID (e.g., xterm16, vt340, grayscale presets).
requirements: builtin_dither must be one of the SIXEL_BUILTIN_* constants.
Returned object must be treated like a dither context; ownership and lifetime of built-ins are not detailed in the header—use without destroying unless documentation says otherwise.

functions.name: sixel_dither_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a dither context object immediately. Prefer unref if using reference counting.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context pointer returned by create/new.
Do not use the pointer after destruction.
Do not destroy objects still referenced elsewhere.

functions.name: sixel_dither_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of a dither context. Thread-unsafe.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.
Caller must ensure thread-safety.
Balance each ref with a corresponding unref.

functions.name: sixel_dither_unref
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of a dither context, destroying it when the count reaches zero. Thread-unsafe.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.
Caller must ensure thread-safety.
After the final unref, the object is destroyed and must not be used.

functions.name: sixel_dither_initialize
functions.signature: SIXELSTATUS sixel_dither_initialize(sixel_dither_t *dither, unsigned char *data, int width, int height, int pixelformat, int method_for_largest, int method_for_rep, int quality_mode);
functions.description: Initializes the dither’s internal palette from a sample pixel buffer, using the specified color quantization and quality settings.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.
data must point to a valid pixel buffer of dimensions width x height in the given pixelformat.
width and height must be positive and within library limits (SIXEL_WIDTH_LIMIT/SIXEL_HEIGHT_LIMIT).
pixelformat must be one of SIXEL_PIXELFORMAT_* constants.
method_for_largest must be one of SIXEL_LARGE_* constants.
method_for_rep must be one of SIXEL_REP_* constants.
quality_mode must be one of SIXEL_QUALITY_* constants.
Returns SIXEL_OK on success; caller must check return value.

functions.name: sixel_dither_set_diffusion_type
functions.description: Sets the error diffusion or dithering method used during encoding.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.
method_for_diffuse must be one of SIXEL_DIFFUSE_* constants.

functions.name: sixel_dither_get_num_of_palette_colors
functions.description: Returns the number of colors in the dither’s current palette.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.

functions.name: sixel_dither_get_num_of_histogram_colors
functions.description: Returns the number of colors observed in the histogram built from initialization data.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.

functions.name: sixel_dither_get_num_of_histgram_colors
functions.description: Deprecated misspelled alias of sixel_dither_get_num_of_histogram_colors. Provided for compatibility.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.

functions.name: sixel_dither_get_palette
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the palette data of the dither context. Format is implementation-defined (comment suggests ARGB/RGBA usage elsewhere).
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.
Caller must not modify unless intended; lifetime is tied to the dither context.

functions.name: sixel_dither_set_palette
functions.description: Sets the palette data used by the dither context.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.
palette must point to a buffer with palette data in the expected format; size and layout are not specified in the header and should match the dither’s expectations.

functions.name: sixel_dither_set_complexion_score
functions.description: Adjusts the complexion color correction factor used during quantization.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.
score must be an integer >= 1 (per header comment).

functions.name: sixel_dither_set_body_only
functions.description: Controls whether to omit the palette definition in the output (body-only mode).
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.
bodyonly must be 0 (output palette section; default) or 1 (omit palette section).

functions.name: sixel_dither_set_optimize_palette
functions.description: Controls palette size optimization.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.
do_opt must be 0 (optimize palette size) or 1 (do not optimize palette size).

functions.name: sixel_dither_set_pixelformat
functions.description: Sets the expected input pixel format for the dither context.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.
pixelformat must be one of SIXEL_PIXELFORMAT_* constants.

functions.name: sixel_dither_set_transparent
functions.description: Sets the transparent color index in the palette.
requirements: dither must be a valid dither context.
transparent is an index into the palette; must be within the current palette range.

functions.name: sixel_encode
functions.signature: SIXELSTATUS sixel_encode(unsigned char *pixels, int width, int height, int depth, sixel_dither_t *dither, sixel_output_t *context);
functions.description: Converts raw pixel data to SIXEL and writes it via the provided output context using the given dither settings.
requirements: pixels must point to a valid pixel buffer with dimensions width x height.
width and height must be positive and within library limits (SIXEL_WIDTH_LIMIT/SIXEL_HEIGHT_LIMIT).
depth argument is currently unused but must be provided; value is ignored per comment.
dither must be a valid dither context (may control palette/diffusion).
context must be a valid output context with a working write callback.
Returns SIXEL_OK on success; caller must check the result.

functions.name: sixel_decode_raw
functions.signature: SIXELSTATUS sixel_decode_raw(unsigned char *p, int len, unsigned char **pixels, int *pwidth, int *pheight, unsigned char **palette, int *ncolors, sixel_allocator_t *allocator);
functions.description: Decodes SIXEL data into indexed pixel bytes and an ARGB palette. Outputs image dimensions and palette size.
requirements: p must point to the SIXEL byte stream; len is its size in bytes.
pixels must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive allocated decoded pixels; memory is allocated via allocator/default and must be freed appropriately.
pwidth and pheight must be valid pointers to receive image dimensions.
palette must be a valid pointer to receive allocated ARGB palette data.
ncolors must be a valid pointer to receive palette size (<= 256 as noted).
allocator may be NULL to use default or a valid allocator object.
Returns SIXEL_OK on success; caller must check return value.

functions.name: sixel_decode
functions.signature: __attribute__((deprecated)) SIXELSTATUS sixel_decode(unsigned char *sixels, int size, unsigned char **pixels, int *pwidth, int *pheight, unsigned char **palette, int *ncolors, sixel_allocator_function fn_malloc);
functions.description: Deprecated decoder that converts SIXEL to indexed pixels and an RGBA palette, allocating via the provided malloc function.
requirements: sixels points to the SIXEL data; size is its length.
pixels, pwidth, pheight, palette, ncolors must be valid pointers for outputs.
ncolors output will be <= 256 (per comment).
fn_malloc must be a valid allocator function or NULL if implementation allows; header shows it is required.
Returns SIXEL_OK on success; caller must check result.

functions.name: sixel_helper_set_additional_message
functions.description: Sets an additional message string used by helper error reporting functions.
requirements: message is a C string pointer; may be NULL to clear depending on implementation (not specified).

functions.name: sixel_helper_get_additional_message
functions.description: Returns the additional message string previously set for error reporting.
requirements: No inputs. Returns a const pointer; caller must not free or modify.

functions.name: sixel_helper_format_error
functions.description: Formats a SIXELSTATUS code into a human-readable string.
requirements: status must be a valid SIXELSTATUS value.
Returns a const C string; caller must not free or modify.

functions.name: sixel_helper_compute_depth
functions.description: Computes the pixel depth (bits per pixel) from a SIXEL pixel format constant.
requirements: pixelformat must be one of SIXEL_PIXELFORMAT_* constants.

functions.name: sixel_helper_normalize_pixelformat
functions.signature: SIXELSTATUS sixel_helper_normalize_pixelformat(unsigned char *dst, int *dst_pixelformat, unsigned char const *src, int src_pixelformat, int width, int height);
functions.description: Converts pixel data from src_pixelformat to a normalized PIXELFORMAT_RGB888, writing to dst and reporting the resulting pixelformat.
requirements: dst must point to a buffer large enough to hold the converted data for width x height in RGB888.
dst_pixelformat must be a valid pointer to receive the converted pixelformat.
src must point to source pixels in src_pixelformat.
src_pixelformat must be one of SIXEL_PIXELFORMAT_* constants.
width and height must be positive and within limits.
Returns SIXEL_OK on success; caller must check result.

functions.name: sixel_helper_scale_image
functions.signature: SIXELSTATUS sixel_helper_scale_image(unsigned char *dst, unsigned char const *src, int srcw, int srch, int pixelformat, int dstw, int dsth, int method_for_resampling, sixel_allocator_t *allocator);
functions.description: Scales an image buffer from srcw x srch to dstw x dsth using the specified resampling filter.
requirements: dst must point to a buffer large enough for the scaled image in the given pixelformat.
src must point to valid source image data of dimensions srcw x srch.
srcw, srch, dstw, dsth must be positive and within limits.
pixelformat must be one of SIXEL_PIXELFORMAT_* constants.
method_for_resampling must be one of SIXEL_RES_* constants.
allocator must be a valid allocator or NULL to use the default.
Returns SIXEL_OK on success; caller must check result.

functions.name: sixel_frame_new
functions.description: Creates a frame object representing a single image frame, optionally using a custom allocator.
requirements: ppframe must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the frame object.
allocator may be NULL to use default or a valid allocator object.
Returns SIXEL_OK on success; caller must check and later unref/destroy the frame.

functions.name: sixel_frame_create
functions.description: Deprecated constructor for a frame object using default allocation. Prefer sixel_frame_new.
requirements: Returns NULL on failure; caller must check and later unref/destroy the frame.

functions.name: sixel_frame_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of a frame object. Thread-unsafe.
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object.
Caller must ensure thread-safety.
Balance each ref with an unref.

functions.name: sixel_frame_unref
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of a frame object, destroying it when the count reaches zero. Thread-unsafe.
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object.
Caller must ensure thread-safety.
After the final unref, the object is destroyed and must not be used.

functions.name: sixel_frame_init
functions.signature: SIXELSTATUS sixel_frame_init(sixel_frame_t *frame, unsigned char *pixels, int width, int height, int pixelformat, unsigned char *palette, int ncolors);
functions.description: Initializes a frame with a pixel buffer, dimensions, pixel format, and optional palette.
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object created beforehand.
pixels must point to the pixel buffer matching width x height and pixelformat.
width and height must be positive and within limits.
pixelformat must be one of SIXEL_PIXELFORMAT_* constants.
palette may be NULL or point to a palette matching pixelformat requirements.
ncolors is the number of palette colors or -1; if not -1, must be within supported range (<= 256).
Returns SIXEL_OK on success; caller must check result.

functions.name: sixel_frame_get_pixels
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the frame’s pixel buffer.
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object.
Returned pointer remains valid while the frame exists and is not reinitialized.

functions.name: sixel_frame_get_palette
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the frame’s palette data, if any.
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object.

functions.name: sixel_frame_get_width
functions.description: Returns the width of the frame in pixels.
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object.

functions.name: sixel_frame_get_height
functions.description: Returns the height of the frame in pixels.
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object.

functions.name: sixel_frame_get_ncolors
functions.description: Returns the number of palette colors for the frame, if applicable.
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object.

functions.name: sixel_frame_get_pixelformat
functions.description: Returns the pixel format of the frame (SIXEL_PIXELFORMAT_*).
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object.

functions.name: sixel_frame_get_transparent
functions.description: Returns the transparent color index for the frame’s palette, if set.
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object.

functions.name: sixel_frame_get_multiframe
functions.description: Returns whether the source data indicates multiple frames (e.g., animation).
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object.

functions.name: sixel_frame_get_delay
functions.description: Returns the inter-frame delay for animated content, typically in centiseconds.
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object.

functions.name: sixel_frame_get_frame_no
functions.description: Returns the frame number within a sequence.
requirements: frame must be a valid frame object.

import random
import struct
from typing import Tuple

# This generator produces valid raw pixel buffers suitable for the fuzz stubs which
# request FUZZ_PARAM_STR as pixel data for various pixelformats:
# - RGB888 (3 bpp)
# - RGBA8888 (4 bpp)
# - ARGB8888 (4 bpp)
# - G8 (1 bpp grayscale)
# - PAL8 (1 bpp indices; palette bytes are also taken from the same blob in stubs)
# - RGB565 (2 bpp, little-endian 5:6:5)
#
# The stubs derive width/height so that width*height*bpp fits exactly in the blob,
# so our task is to return a bytes object whose length is compatible with many bpp
# choices and yields interesting imagery (gradients, patterns, edges, transparency, etc.).
#
# Strategy:
# - Randomly choose a pixelformat family and small-ish dimensions (<= 128) to keep size small.
# - Synthesize pixels matching that format, with varied patterns:
#     * color/gray ramps, checkerboards, stripes, alpha gradients, random speckles
# - Sometimes append an extra region of bytes to allow the fuzzers to pick different
#   width/height combos from the same blob while still having enough data.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

# Supported formats and their bytes-per-pixel
FORMATS = [
    ("RGB888", 3),
    ("RGBA8888", 4),
    ("ARGB8888", 4),
    ("G8", 1),
    ("PAL8", 1),
    ("RGB565", 2),
]


def _mk_dims(rng: random.Random, bpp: int, max_bytes: int = 4096) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    # Prefer square-ish or slightly rectangular images, ensure at least 1x1
    # Cap width/height to keep width*height*bpp <= max_bytes
    # Try several attempts to find a pleasant dimension
    for _ in range(20):
        base = rng.randint(8, 128)
        aspect = rng.choice([(1, 1), (2, 1), (1, 2), (4, 3), (3, 4)])
        w = max(1, (base * aspect[0]) // aspect[1])
        h = max(1, (base * aspect[1]) // aspect[0])
        # Clip to 1..1024 like stubs
        w = min(w, 1024)
        h = min(h, 1024)
        if w * h * bpp <= max_bytes:
            return w, h
    # Fallback tiny dims
    w = rng.randint(1, 64)
    h = max(1, min(64, max_bytes // max(1, w * bpp)))
    if h < 1:
        h = 1
    return w, h


def _pack_rgb565(r: int, g: int, b: int) -> bytes:
    # Convert 8-bit RGB to little-endian 5:6:5
    r5 = (r * 31 + 127) // 255
    g6 = (g * 63 + 127) // 255
    b5 = (b * 31 + 127) // 255
    val = (r5 << 11) | (g6 << 5) | b5
    return struct.pack('<H', val)


def _gen_pattern(rng: random.Random, fmt: str, w: int, h: int) -> bytes:
    bpp = {
        "RGB888": 3,
        "RGBA8888": 4,
        "ARGB8888": 4,
        "G8": 1,
        "PAL8": 1,
        "RGB565": 2,
    }[fmt]

    # Choose a visual pattern
    pattern = rng.choice([
        "gradient_xy",
        "checker",
        "stripes_h",
        "stripes_v",
        "alpha_diag",
        "speckle",
    ])

    buf = bytearray()
    for y in range(h):
        for x in range(w):
            # Base color components as 0..255
            if pattern == "gradient_xy":
                r = (x * 255) // max(1, w - 1)
                g = (y * 255) // max(1, h - 1)
                b = ((x + y) * 255) // max(1, w + h - 2)
                a = (x ^ y) & 0xFF
            elif pattern == "checker":
                cell = 8 + rng.randint(0, 8)
                v = 255 if ((x // cell) ^ (y // cell)) & 1 else 32
                r = v
                g = 255 - v
                b = (v // 2)
                a = 255
            elif pattern == "stripes_h":
                v = (y * 255) // max(1, h - 1)
                r = v
                g = 255 - v
                b = (v // 2)
                a = 255
            elif pattern == "stripes_v":
                v = (x * 255) // max(1, w - 1)
                r = 255 - v
                g = v
                b = (v // 3)
                a = 255
            elif pattern == "alpha_diag":
                r = (x * 255) // max(1, w - 1)
                g = (y * 255) // max(1, h - 1)
                b = 200
                a = ((x + y) * 255) // max(1, w + h - 2)
            else:  # speckle
                r = rng.randrange(256)
                g = rng.randrange(256)
                b = rng.randrange(256)
                a = rng.randrange(256)

            if fmt == "RGB888":
                buf += bytes((r, g, b))
            elif fmt == "RGBA8888":
                buf += bytes((r, g, b, a))
            elif fmt == "ARGB8888":
                buf += bytes((a, r, g, b))
            elif fmt == "G8":
                # Luma approximation
                y8 = (299 * r + 587 * g + 114 * b + 500) // 1000
                buf.append(y8 & 0xFF)
            elif fmt == "PAL8":
                # Create index using a small repeating palette space 0..n-1
                # The fuzzer may set ncolors later; keep indices in 0..255.
                # Use combined XY to exercise palette range
                idx = (x + 3 * y) & 0xFF
                buf.append(idx)
            elif fmt == "RGB565":
                buf += _pack_rgb565(r, g, b)
    return bytes(buf)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a primary format likely to match the stubs' selections
    fmt, bpp = rng.choice(FORMATS)

    # Reserve some budget to optionally append extra data tail for palette reuse etc.
    # Keep overall size <= 4096.
    w, h = _mk_dims(rng, bpp, max_bytes=4096)

    payload = bytearray(_gen_pattern(rng, fmt, w, h))

    # Optionally append additional blocks in other formats to let different stubs
    # reuse the same blob for different bpp without bailing, while staying valid.
    # Each block is self-contained valid pixels for its own implicit dims, but the
    # stubs only require that width*height*bpp fits within blob; they pick dims from size.
    # We just ensure the blob has ample bytes. Do not exceed 4096.
    maybe_append = rng.random() < 0.7
    if maybe_append:
        # Append a small RGB888 gradient or a tiny palette chunk-like block
        extra_fmt = rng.choice(["RGB888", "G8", "RGB565"])  # safe common formats
        extra_bpp = {"RGB888": 3, "G8": 1, "RGB565": 2}[extra_fmt]
        # Generate very small block to keep under cap
        ew, eh = _mk_dims(rng, extra_bpp, max_bytes=1024)
        extra = _gen_pattern(rng, extra_fmt, ew, eh)
        # Truncate if needed to keep total <= 4096
        space = 4096 - len(payload)
        if space > 0:
            payload += extra[:space]

    # Ensure non-empty
    if not payload:
        payload = bytearray(b"\x00")

    return bytes(payload)

import random
from typing import List

# Generator for palette bytes suitable for libsixel contexts.
# We produce non-empty bytes with plausible palette layouts and sizes.
# Focus on typical palette encodings used by libsixel APIs:
# - ARGB8888 (4 bytes/entry)
# - RGBA8888 (4 bytes/entry)
# - RGB888 (3 bytes/entry) sometimes accepted/used
# - Grayscale ramps (1 byte intensity expanded to 3/4 bytes)
# - VT340/xterm-like 16/256 color palettes
# Ensures length > 0 so fuzz stubs do not bail on empty strings.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

# Some well-known palettes (partial) to seed variety
XTERM_16 = [
    (0, 0, 0), (205, 0, 0), (0, 205, 0), (205, 205, 0),
    (0, 0, 238), (205, 0, 205), (0, 205, 205), (229, 229, 229),
    (127, 127, 127), (255, 0, 0), (0, 255, 0), (255, 255, 0),
    (92, 92, 255), (255, 0, 255), (0, 255, 255), (255, 255, 255),
]

# Standard 6x6x6 cube + 16 gray levels for xterm256
def build_xterm256() -> List[tuple]:
    pal: List[tuple] = []
    # 16 ANSI colors first (approx; reuse XTERM_16)
    pal.extend(XTERM_16)
    # 6x6x6 cube
    steps = [0, 95, 135, 175, 215, 255]
    for r in steps:
        for g in steps:
            for b in steps:
                pal.append((r, g, b))
    # 24 grayscale ramp (8..238 step 10)
    for v in [8 + i * 10 for i in range(24)]:
        pal.append((v, v, v))
    return pal[:256]

XTERM_256 = build_xterm256()


def clamp(n, lo, hi):
    return lo if n < lo else hi if n > hi else n


def choose(entries_range: range, rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # favor common sizes: 16, 32, 64, 128, 256
    common = [16, 32, 64, 128, 256]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        c = rng.choice(common)
        if c in entries_range:
            return c
    return rng.choice(list(entries_range))


def to_bytes_rgb888(pal: List[tuple]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for r, g, b in pal:
        out.extend((r & 0xFF, g & 0xFF, b & 0xFF))
    return bytes(out)


def to_bytes_rgba8888(pal: List[tuple], alpha_mode: str, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for r, g, b in pal:
        if alpha_mode == "opaque":
            a = 255
        elif alpha_mode == "binary":
            a = 255 if rng.random() < 0.85 else 0
        else:  # gradient
            a = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        out.extend((r & 0xFF, g & 0xFF, b & 0xFF, a & 0xFF))
    return bytes(out)


def to_bytes_argb8888(pal: List[tuple], alpha_mode: str, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for r, g, b in pal:
        if alpha_mode == "opaque":
            a = 255
        elif alpha_mode == "binary":
            a = 255 if rng.random() < 0.85 else 0
        else:
            a = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        out.extend((a & 0xFF, r & 0xFF, g & 0xFF, b & 0xFF))
    return bytes(out)


def build_grayscale(n: int) -> List[tuple]:
    if n <= 1:
        return [(0, 0, 0)]
    pal = []
    for i in range(n):
        v = clamp(round(i * 255 / (n - 1)), 0, 255)
        pal.append((v, v, v))
    return pal


def build_random_palette(n: int, rng: random.Random, biased: bool = False) -> List[tuple]:
    pal = []
    if biased and n >= 6:
        # include some primaries and common UI colors first
        seeds = [(0,0,0),(255,255,255),(255,0,0),(0,255,0),(0,0,255),(255,255,0),(0,255,255),(255,0,255)]
        for c in seeds[: min(len(seeds), n)]:
            pal.append(c)
    while len(pal) < n:
        # bias towards full saturation and gray occasionally
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            v = rng.randrange(0, 256)
            c = (v, v, v)
        else:
            r = rng.randrange(0, 256)
            g = rng.randrange(0, 256)
            b = rng.randrange(0, 256)
            c = (r, g, b)
        pal.append(c)
    return pal


def cap_to_max(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(data) <= MAX_BYTES:
        return data
    return data[:MAX_BYTES]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Strategy selection
    # 0: XTERM16 RGB
    # 1: XTERM256 RGB
    # 2: Random palette RGB888
    # 3: Random palette RGBA8888
    # 4: Random palette ARGB8888
    # 5: Grayscale RGB888
    # 6: Small alpha palette RGBA8888
    strategy = rng.choices(population=list(range(7)), weights=[1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 2, 2], k=1)[0]

    # Determine number of entries (1..256). For pal8, up to 256 colors typical.
    entries = choose(range(1, 257), rng)

    if strategy == 0:
        pal = XTERM_16[:entries]
        data = to_bytes_rgb888(pal)
    elif strategy == 1:
        pal = XTERM_256[:entries]
        data = to_bytes_rgb888(pal)
    elif strategy == 2:
        pal = build_random_palette(entries, rng, biased=True)
        data = to_bytes_rgb888(pal)
    elif strategy == 3:
        pal = build_random_palette(entries, rng, biased=True)
        alpha_mode = rng.choice(["opaque", "binary", "gradient"])
        data = to_bytes_rgba8888(pal, alpha_mode, rng)
    elif strategy == 4:
        pal = build_random_palette(entries, rng, biased=False)
        alpha_mode = rng.choice(["opaque", "binary", "gradient"])
        data = to_bytes_argb8888(pal, alpha_mode, rng)
    elif strategy == 5:
        pal = build_grayscale(entries)
        data = to_bytes_rgb888(pal)
    else:  # strategy == 6
        # Favor small palettes with varied alpha for testing transparency handling
        entries = min(entries, rng.choice([2, 4, 8, 16, 32]))
        pal = build_random_palette(entries, rng, biased=True)
        data = to_bytes_rgba8888(pal, alpha_mode="binary", rng=rng)

    # Guarantee non-empty and within limit
    if not data:
        # Fallback: single opaque white entry RGBA
        data = bytes([255, 255, 255, 255])

    data = cap_to_max(data)
    return data

import random
from typing import List

# SIXEL byte stream generator
# We aim to produce valid, decodable SIXEL sequences that exercise palette definition,
# color selection, run-lengths, and multiple lines. Keep under 4096 bytes.

CSI_7BIT = "\x1b["
DCS_7BIT = "\x1bP"
ST_7BIT = "\x1b\\"

# SIXEL syntax helpers
# Basic structure: DCS "0;0;8q" <raster attrs> <palette> <data> ST
# - Introducer: "0;0;8q" selects sixel mode
# - Raster attributes (optional): '"' P1;P2;P3;P4 where width,height, ...
# - Palette: '#<index>;2;<r>;<g>;<b>' with r,g,b in 0..100
# - Data: '!<n><c>' repeats char c (63..118 corresponds to pixel columns), '$' CR, '-' NL


def clamp(v, lo, hi):
    return max(lo, min(hi, v))


def gen_palette(n: int, rnd: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Define up to 256 palette entries using both 100-scale and some edge values
    cmds = []
    used = min(256, max(1, n))
    for i in range(used):
        # Mix of deterministic and random colors within 0..100 scale
        if i == 0:
            r, g, b = 0, 0, 0
        elif i == 1:
            r, g, b = 100, 100, 100
        elif i == 2:
            r, g, b = 100, 0, 0
        elif i == 3:
            r, g, b = 0, 100, 0
        elif i == 4:
            r, g, b = 0, 0, 100
        else:
            r = rnd.randrange(0, 101)
            g = rnd.randrange(0, 101)
            b = rnd.randrange(0, 101)
        cmds.append(f"#{i};2;{r};{g};{b}")
    return cmds


def sixel_repeat(n: int, ch: int) -> str:
    # '!n<ch>' where n is 1..255 typically, but some decoders accept larger; keep in 1..255
    n = clamp(n, 1, 255)
    return f"!{n}{chr(ch)}"


def gen_sixel_lines(width: int, height: int, colors: List[int], rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build sixel bitmap lines; each line represents 6 pixel rows
    # We'll generate height rows using '-' to move to next 6-row band
    # For each band, we select a color with '#' and emit runs across columns
    cols = clamp(width, 1, 800)  # keep sane
    bands = max(1, (height + 5) // 6)
    out = []

    for band in range(bands):
        # For each color in a small set per band
        band_colors = rnd.sample(colors, k=min(len(colors), rnd.randint(1, min(4, len(colors)))))
        for ci, color in enumerate(band_colors):
            out.append(f"#{color}")
            # Occasionally use CR within the same band to exercise '$'
            remaining = cols
            first_segment = True
            while remaining > 0:
                seg = rnd.randint(1, min(64, remaining))
                ch = rnd.randint(63, 118)  # valid data chars
                out.append(sixel_repeat(seg, ch))
                remaining -= seg
                # Insert a carriage return between color planes sometimes
                if first_segment and rnd.random() < 0.2 and remaining > 0:
                    out.append("$")
                first_segment = False
        # Move to next sixel band (newline)
        if band != bands - 1:
            out.append("-")
    return ''.join(out)


def gen_raster_attr(w: int, h: int) -> str:
    # '"' P1;P2;P3;P4  -> width;height;horz pixel aspect;vert pixel aspect
    # Use 1:1 aspect most times
    return f'"{w};{h};1;1'


def gen_header(rnd: random.Random, use_8bit: bool) -> str:
    # Use 7-bit DCS/ST for portability
    intro_params = []
    # P1: 0 -> normal, 1 -> transparent background often used
    p1 = rnd.choice([0, 1])
    p2 = rnd.choice([0, 1])
    p3 = 8  # sixel
    intro_params = f"{p1};{p2};{p3}q"
    return DCS_7BIT + intro_params


def gen_trailer() -> str:
    return ST_7BIT


def gen_sixel(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Random image geometry within typical limits
    width = rnd.randint(8, 160)
    height = rnd.randint(6, 120)

    # Choose palette size and active colors
    palette_size = rnd.choice([2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256])
    palette_cmds = gen_palette(palette_size, rnd)

    # Select a subset of colors to actually use in bitmap runs
    use_colors = list(range(palette_size))
    rnd.shuffle(use_colors)
    active_colors = use_colors[:rnd.randint(1, min(10, palette_size))]

    # Construct stream
    parts: List[str] = []
    parts.append(gen_header(rnd, use_8bit=False))

    # Occasionally include raster attributes first
    if rnd.random() < 0.9:
        parts.append(gen_raster_attr(width, height))

    # Emit some palette definitions
    # Emit in multiple chunks to exercise parser states
    if palette_size <= 16:
        parts.extend(palette_cmds)
    else:
        # Split into groups
        idx = 0
        while idx < len(palette_cmds):
            chunk = rnd.randint(4, 32)
            parts.extend(palette_cmds[idx:idx+chunk])
            idx += chunk
            if idx < len(palette_cmds) and rnd.random() < 0.2:
                # interleave a no-op data line: select a color and zero/short run
                parts.append(f"#{active_colors[0]}")
                parts.append(sixel_repeat(1, rnd.randint(63, 118)))
                parts.append("-")

    # Main bitmap data
    parts.append(gen_sixel_lines(width, height, active_colors, rnd))

    # Trailer
    parts.append(gen_trailer())

    data = ''.join(parts).encode('ascii', errors='strict')
    # Cap to 4096 bytes as per requirement
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    return gen_sixel(seed)

import random
import struct
import zlib

# This generator produces valid image file contents for common formats that the
# target accepts via filename inputs: PNG, GIF87a/89a, BMP, PNM (P6), and SIXEL.
# It randomly chooses a tiny but valid image in one of these formats to exercise
# different decoding paths. All outputs are <= 4096 bytes.

# Utility: pack little-endian
le16 = lambda v: struct.pack('<H', v)
le32 = lambda v: struct.pack('<I', v)
be16 = lambda v: struct.pack('>H', v)
be32 = lambda v: struct.pack('>I', v)


def crc32(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def chunk_png(typ: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return be32(len(data)) + typ + data + crc32(typ + data)


def gen_png_small(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a minimal valid PNG with IHDR, IDAT, IEND.
    # Randomize: tiny dimensions (1..8), color types (2 RGB, 6 RGBA, 0 grayscale, 4 GA), bit depth 8
    width = rng.randint(1, 8)
    height = rng.randint(1, 8)
    color_type = rng.choice([0, 2, 4, 6])
    bit_depth = 8
    # PNG requires certain color type + bit depth combos to be valid: 8 with 0/2/4/6 is valid.
    compression = 0
    filter_method = 0
    interlace = rng.choice([0, 1])

    ihdr = be32(width) + be32(height) + bytes([bit_depth, color_type, compression, filter_method, interlace])

    # Build raw scanlines with filter byte 0 per row.
    if color_type == 0:
        cpp = 1  # gray8
        def pixel():
            return bytes([rng.randrange(256)])
    elif color_type == 2:
        cpp = 3  # RGB
        def pixel():
            return bytes([rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256)])
    elif color_type == 4:
        cpp = 2  # GA
        def pixel():
            return bytes([rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256)])
    else:  # 6 RGBA
        cpp = 4
        def pixel():
            return bytes([rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256)])

    raw = bytearray()
    for _y in range(height):
        raw.append(0)  # filter type 0
        # Ensure at least plausible content variation
        row = bytearray()
        for _x in range(width):
            row += pixel()
        raw += row

    idat = zlib.compress(bytes(raw), level=rng.choice([0, 1, 6, 9]))

    png = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + chunk_png(b'IHDR', ihdr) + chunk_png(b'IDAT', idat) + chunk_png(b'IEND', b'')
    return png


def gen_gif_small(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal GIF87a/89a with a global color table and a small image (1..8)^2
    width = rng.randint(1, 16)
    height = rng.randint(1, 16)
    version = rng.choice([b'GIF87a', b'GIF89a'])
    # Choose color table size: 2^(N+1) colors, N in 0..7
    nbits = rng.randint(0, 3)  # keep small
    num_colors = 1 << (nbits + 1)
    gct_flag = 1
    color_res = 7  # typical
    sort = 0
    gct_size_field = nbits  # maps to size=2^(N+1)

    packed = (gct_flag << 7) | (color_res << 4) | (sort << 3) | gct_size_field
    bg_index = 0
    pixel_aspect = 0

    # Build a global color table
    gct = bytearray()
    for i in range(num_colors):
        gct += bytes([rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256)])

    # Image Descriptor
    left = 0
    top = 0
    lct_flag = 0
    interlace = rng.randint(0, 1)
    sort_lct = 0
    lct_size_field = 0
    img_packed = (lct_flag << 7) | (interlace << 6) | (sort_lct << 5) | lct_size_field

    # Build a simple LZW minimum code size and one data sub-block stream
    lzw_min_code_size = max(2, nbits + 1)

    # Construct a trivial LZW stream: clear code, a few pixel indices, end code
    clear_code = 1 << lzw_min_code_size
    end_code = clear_code + 1
    # Emit a few pixels cycling indices within table
    pixels = [i % num_colors for i in range(width * height)]

    # Pack LZW codes into bytes. We'll do a naive bit-packing with static code size advancing.
    code_size = lzw_min_code_size + 1
    code_stream = []
    code_stream.append(clear_code)
    code_stream.extend(pixels[: min(len(pixels), 32)])
    code_stream.append(end_code)

    # Bit pack
    bitbuf = 0
    bitcnt = 0
    out = bytearray()
    for code in code_stream:
        bitbuf |= (code & ((1 << code_size) - 1)) << bitcnt
        bitcnt += code_size
        while bitcnt >= 8:
            out.append(bitbuf & 0xFF)
            bitbuf >>= 8
            bitcnt -= 8
    if bitcnt:
        out.append(bitbuf & 0xFF)

    # Single sub-block followed by a zero terminator
    image_data = bytes([lzw_min_code_size, len(out)]) + bytes(out) + b"\x00"

    data = bytearray()
    data += version
    data += le16(width) + le16(height)
    data += bytes([packed, bg_index, pixel_aspect])
    data += gct
    # Image Separator
    data += b"\x2C"
    data += le16(left) + le16(top) + le16(width) + le16(height)
    data += bytes([img_packed])
    data += image_data
    # Trailer
    data += b"\x3B"
    return bytes(data)


def gen_bmp_small(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal uncompressed 24-bit BMP (BI_RGB)
    width = rng.randint(1, 32)
    height = rng.randint(1, 32)
    bpp = 24
    row_raw = ((width * (bpp // 8) + 3) // 4) * 4  # padded to 4 bytes
    img_size = row_raw * height

    bfType = b'BM'
    bfOffBits = 14 + 40  # no palette
    bfSize = bfOffBits + img_size

    # BITMAPINFOHEADER
    biSize = 40
    biPlanes = 1
    biCompression = 0  # BI_RGB
    biXPelsPerMeter = 2835
    biYPelsPerMeter = 2835
    biClrUsed = 0
    biClrImportant = 0

    header = bytearray()
    header += bfType
    header += le32(bfSize)
    header += le16(0) + le16(0)
    header += le32(bfOffBits)

    info = bytearray()
    info += le32(biSize)
    info += le32(width)
    info += le32(height)
    info += le16(biPlanes)
    info += le16(bpp)
    info += le32(biCompression)
    info += le32(img_size)
    info += le32(biXPelsPerMeter)
    info += le32(biYPelsPerMeter)
    info += le32(biClrUsed)
    info += le32(biClrImportant)

    # Bottom-up BGR rows with padding
    pixels = bytearray()
    for _y in range(height):
        row = bytearray()
        for _x in range(width):
            row += bytes([rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256)])  # B,G,R
        row += b"\x00" * (row_raw - len(row))
        pixels = row + pixels  # prepend to build bottom-up

    return bytes(header + info + pixels)


def gen_pnm_p6_small(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Binary PPM (P6) with maxval 255
    width = rng.randint(1, 32)
    height = rng.randint(1, 32)
    header = f"P6\n{width} {height}\n255\n".encode('ascii')
    data = bytearray()
    for _ in range(width * height):
        data += bytes([rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256)])
    return header + bytes(data)


def gen_sixel_small(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Generate a minimal valid SIXEL sequence inside DCS ... ST
    # Simple palette with a few colors and a few pixel rows.
    # Reference: ESC P ... ST, use 7-bit sequence.
    ESC = b"\x1b"
    DCS = ESC + b"Pq"  # DCS with 'q' to start SIXEL
    ST = ESC + b"\\"

    # Build a small palette: define color #1 and #2
    # #<n>;2;<r>;<g>;<b> where r,g,b are 0..100
    def color_cmd(idx, r, g, b):
        return f"#{idx};2;{r};{g};{b}".encode('ascii')

    palette = color_cmd(1, rng.randint(0, 100), rng.randint(0, 100), rng.randint(0, 100)) + \
              color_cmd(2, rng.randint(0, 100), rng.randint(0, 100), rng.randint(0, 100))

    # Raster attributes: set pixel aspect (optional). We'll omit for simplicity.

    # Build a few lines using repeat and color select: $ is new line, - is move to next row
    # Use basic patterns with run-length '!' and data bytes '?'..'~' (0x3F..0x7E) map 0..63
    # Select color via #<n>
    lines = []
    width = rng.randint(4, 20)
    rows = rng.randint(2, 6)
    for y in range(rows):
        color = rng.choice([1, 2])
        run1 = rng.randint(1, width)
        run2 = max(1, width - run1)
        # Build sixel row: select color, repeat run1 of pattern '@' (0 maps 0x3F '?', so choose 'A' => 0x41 => value 0x02)
        # We'll stick to '?' (0) and 'o' (0x6F -> 0x30), but any 0..63 is allowed.
        part = []
        part.append(f"#{color}".encode('ascii'))
        part.append(b"!" + str(run1).encode('ascii') + b"?")
        part.append(b"!" + str(run2).encode('ascii') + b"o")
        lines.append(b"".join(part))
    # Combine lines separated by '-' to advance to next 6-pixel row
    body = b"$".join(lines)  # '$' is carriage return in sixel; keep simple
    body = body.replace(b"$", b"")  # simplify to contiguous output
    # Use '-' to move to next row between lines
    body = b"-".join(lines)

    seq = DCS + palette + body + ST
    if len(seq) > 4096:
        seq = seq[:4096]
    return seq


_GENERATORS = [
    gen_png_small,
    gen_gif_small,
    gen_bmp_small,
    gen_pnm_p6_small,
    gen_sixel_small,
]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Weighted choice to frequently produce widely supported formats
    gens = [gen_png_small, gen_gif_small, gen_bmp_small, gen_pnm_p6_small, gen_sixel_small]
    weights = [4, 3, 2, 2, 2]
    gen = rng.choices(gens, weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    data = gen(rng)
    # Ensure within size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
